cohort: The study included 196 pregnant women with pre-eclampsia as cases and 366 age and parity-matched pregnant women without pre-eclampsia as controls, all enrolled in a mental health registry.
finding: Women with pre-eclampsia exhibited significantly higher frequencies of depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, and psychological distress compared to women without pre-eclampsia, and experienced more frequent adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Women with pre-eclampsia experienced higher rates of emergency cesarean sections.
